newsitem.title: USA: AT&T pressures put Allen's leadership to test.
newsitem.headline: AT&T pressures put Allen's leadership to test.

text.p: AT&T Corp, citing pressures in its key long-distance phone business, warned Tuesday that its second half earnings would be disappointing, prompting some analysts to question whether the telecoms leviathan is nimble enough to face the bruising era of competition ahead.
The surprise earnings forecast raised new concerns about current management among analysts who wonder whether AT&T will be able to turn the corner under Chairman Robert Allen.

In a move to battle back, the telecommunications behemoth also launched a new long-distance program, joining the ranks of rivals Sprint Corp and MCI Communications Corp to offer a less-complicated, fixed-rate residential pricing structure.
AT&T said its third-quarter earnings could be as much as 10 percent below Wall Street estimates and that the pressure would continue for the rest of the year.
The news sparked a sell-off in the company's stock, which is the most widely held in North America.
